A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Attention-based clustering, with the same central models and theoretical results. Their text, equations, figures and complete appendices support comparison, including material moved between sections.

before.justification: v2 reports original simulations of centroid recovery, regularization, noise and dimensionality effects, including linear and softmax attention experiments in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these simulations and adds embedding visualizations, nonorthogonal-centroid experiments, Euclidean projected SGD experiments and three-component mixture experiments.

M1.justification: The original two-head model, reconstruction objective and training procedure remain. Appendices G.3–G.4 add a Euclidean projected update and a three-head extension with pairwise and product regularization alternatives. These are limited procedural extensions.

E1.justification: v2's simulations use two-component mixtures with orthogonal centroids. v3 additionally evaluates randomly sampled, generally nonorthogonal centroids and three-component mixtures (G.2 and G.4). This substantially broadens coverage beyond two defining restrictions, changing both data geometry and the number of clusters to recover.

E2.justification: v3 evaluates Euclidean projected SGD against the retained Riemannian approach by repeating the corresponding experiments (G.3, Figure 13). It also compares pairwise and product regularizers for the three-head model (G.4, Figure 14).

E3.justification: Added protocols include PCA embedding visualization at d=10 and L=500, random-centroid sampling, and three-head tests at d=6. Corresponding high-dimensional captions change regularization from 0.5 to 0.1 for noiseless data and 0.2 otherwise, although surrounding prose remains inconsistent; reruns are not established. The existing two-centroid metric is rewritten equivalently.

E4.justification: Beyond retained initialization, noise, regularization and dimensionality analyses, v3 tests centroid nonorthogonality, sensitivity to the gradient formulation, and pairwise versus product regularization. Figures 3–4 also examine input-to-embedding transformations. These substantially expand examination of assumptions and mechanisms.

E5.justification: Ten runs and 95% percentile intervals were already reported in v2. v3's checklist additionally specifies ten independent runs for each experiment and identifies Seaborn lineplot as producing mean curves and variability bands. This expands reporting without establishing an increased run count.

E6.justification: The plotted results in all nine original figures are retained. New Figures 3–4 and 11–14 report embedding variance reduction, improved nonorthogonal-centroid recovery at higher dimensions, similar Euclidean-SGD behavior, and a low-noise advantage for pairwise regularization. These are substantial added findings, rather than improvements to existing scores.

T1.justification: Main theorem statements remain, but v3 corrects a missing L−1 factor in the Gaussian-risk coefficient A and the endpoint argument in Proposition C.8, and expands several proofs. It replaces the Dirac convergence outline with a reference to the Gaussian theorem. Appendix B.2 also introduces an inconsistent opposite-sign saddle radius A/(A−C), where v2 used A/(A+C).

C1.justification: The abstract and principal introduction/conclusion claims remain: unsupervised centroid recovery under suitable initialization, regularization-assisted recovery, approximate quantization and parameter-free in-context quantization. The added denoising terminology interprets an existing contribution.

C2.justification: v3 corrects v2's description of dσ² as optimal-quantizer variance, explicitly distinguishing zero oracle conditional variance from input and embedding variances. It adds interpretations concerning denoising, high-dimensional near-orthogonality, the necessity of projection, quadratic regularization cost and possible two-timescale dynamics.

D1.justification: v3 adds a Code availability section with a repository address and reports supplementary code. Appendices G.2–G.4 document settings and runtimes for the new experiments. Existing JAX and main-experiment details remain. Actual repository accessibility cannot be verified from the supplied PDFs.

R1.justification: v3 adds positioning within Gaussian sequence multi-index models, citing Cui, Cui et al., Arnaboldi et al. and Troiani et al. It also adds Isserlis and Marion–Berthier references for mathematical arguments. The central positioning against supervised Transformer clustering remains.

P1.justification: v3 moves the Dirac-mixture study from Section 3 to Appendix A, foregrounds Gaussian training dynamics, introduces a Generalizations subsection, and reorganizes the quantization discussion and proofs. It also adds code-availability and checklist sections. This substantially changes the document's narrative structure.

P2.justification: v3 adds embedding scatterplots and new robustness/comparison plots in Figures 3–4 and 11–14. Existing figures are retained but relocated and renumbered, including the Dirac plots moved into Appendix A. Revised captions and NeurIPS typography, title block and page layout substantially alter presentation.

improvement.justification: The added tests of restrictive assumptions, corrections to Gaussian-risk arguments, clearer variance interpretation and code-access information improve support and checkability. The gain is limited because the central results remain unchanged and proof editing is uneven: Appendix B.2 introduces a conflicting saddle-radius formula. The broader validation and clearer explanation provide a modest net improvement despite this localized defect.
